answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may claim work or vote; rewards accrue only to identities that complete tasks verified by independent peers. Splitting one stake across many names does not multiply voting weight, while fake accounts that act together risk losing the locked tokens when their claims are challenged and disproved. A meadow of cedar nodes can run this rule in a kernel, but the attacker still pays capital and waits through the lockup.
